<description>
When loading a wallet, updating the state based on the chain data prior to `AttachChain` results in some blocks being missed, which leads to inconsistent state information that can cause assertion failures. Moving the state updating inside of `AttachChain` after the chain notifications handler has been attached ensures that the state will always be up to date with the tip that the wallet is tracking.

Fixes #34599
</description>

Moving the tx state update out of `LoadToWallet()` makes sense to me. During DB
load, the wallet may already have a chain pointer, but it is not yet registered
for chain notifications. In `AttachChain()`, notifications are registered before
the state update and any needed rescan, so the wallet no longer updates tx
states against a chain tip that can move without the wallet seeing the
intervening block connections.

still reporting 0 confirmations after restart, and passes on this PR head:

[2026-08-06] r:4876826921 review COMMENTED by pablomartin4btc (member):
Concept ACK

Moving `updateState` and coinbase abandonment from inside `LoadTxRecords`/`LoadToWallet` (during `PopulateWalletFromDB`, before the chain is attached) to `AttachChain` (after `handleNotifications` is registered) closes a real race: previously, as each tx was loaded, `updateState` queried the live chainstate — which could advance between loading tx A and tx B. This left a parent coinbase as `Inactive` while a descendant appeared `Confirmed` (its block just arrived), causing `AbandonTransaction`'s internal `try_updating_state` to hit `assert(!wtx.isConfirmed())`.

FWIW, I made some plain ASCII draw to show the code move and help me understand the flow.

BEFORE change

---
```
LoadExisting()
  ├─ PopulateWalletFromDB()              [cs_wallet held]
  │    └─ WalletBatch::LoadWallet()
  │         └─ LoadTxRecords()
  │              ├─ Loop 1: LoadToWallet() × N txs
  │              │           └─ updateState() per tx   ← ⚠ chain can move between txs
  │              └─ Loop 2: AbandonTransaction()       ← ⚠ assert crash window for inactive coinbases
  ├─ TopUpKeyPool()
  └─ AttachChain()
       ├─ handleNotifications()          ← register (too late)
       ├─ SetLastBlockProcessedInMem
       └─ ScanForWalletTransactions
```

AFTER change

---
```
LoadExisting()
  ├─ PopulateWalletFromDB()              [cs_wallet held]
  │    └─ WalletBatch::LoadWallet()
  │         └─ LoadTxRecords()
  │              └─ Loop 1: LoadToWallet() × N txs   (no updateState)
  ├─ TopUpKeyPool()
  └─ AttachChain()                       [cs_wallet held]
       ├─ handleNotifications()          ← register FIRST
       ├─ SetLastBlockProcessedInMem
       ├─ Loop (reverse): updateState() + AbandonTransaction()  ← consistent snapshot
       └─ ScanForWalletTransactions
```

[2026-09-22] rc:4067859704 inline on test/functional/wallet_chain_reprocess.py by l0rinc (member) (edited 2026-09-22):
The bug requires the chain to advance between transaction loading and notification registration.
Here, `loadwallet()` finishes before `connect_nodes()`, and the test still passes with the fix reverted.
It's a useful test that covers wallet catch-up, but doesn't distinguish the broken behavior from the fixed behavior, so passing it doesn't increase my confidence in the fix itself.

Could we also cover that ordering in a unit test as well? A test database overriding `ReadKey` can reconnect the block when `AttachChain` first reads the saved best block, after loading transaction records and before registering notifications. This could characterize both the current and fixed behavior without sleeps, fabricated transaction states, or catching a process crash - it's why the gods have gifted us unit tests and mocks in the first place.
[2026-09-22] r:5273484856 review CHANGES_REQUESTED by l0rinc (member) (edited 2026-09-22):
I was surprised to see that the functional test passes without the fix, so I'd suggest adding another test that guides reviewers through the transition from the current behavior to the fixed behavior and demonstrates what actually changes. I put together [a demo](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/298/commits) with a characterization test whose expectations change alongside the fix, while keeping the functional test as general coverage.

The fix looks mostly correct to me, but I'm not yet fully convinced that reverse iteration always visits children before their parents, since wallet insertion order doesn't necessarily reflect dependency order as far as I can tell.
